Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we’re aligned on scope and timeline: 

POC goal (what success looks like)
- End-to-end integration of Redwood text generation into Acme Support Assist for a single product line (webchat).
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for 512-token requests during business hours.
- Cost: average per request cost target <= $0.012 after batching/caching.
- Quality: F1/accuracy on the curated eval set >= 88% (Priya will share eval set).

Evaluation plan
- Acme provides a representative prompt set + acceptance evals (Priya).
- Redwood will run a baseline with the proposed model and provide token-level cost/latency report.
- Weekly sync to review logs, failure modes, and prompt tweaks.

Timeline & ownership
- Week 0 (this week): sign MOU for trial scope & data handling (Jordan).
- Week 1: dev kickoff, SDK integration (Acme engs + Dev Patel).
- Week 2: internal test harness + streaming validation (Redwood).
- Week 3: live trial on small percentage of traffic, measure SLOs (both).

Immediate next steps
1) I’ve attached an integration checklist and a proposed success-criteria doc. Please confirm owners and sign-off on the MOU draft.
2) Dev — can you confirm SDK compatibility with Acme’s JavaScript stack and note any blockers?
3) Jordan/Priya — what’s your preferred day next week for a 30-min integration kickoff?

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (integration checklist), acme-poc-success-criteria.docx

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Jordan — thanks, and good question on the latency metric. For the POC success criteria we should define both:
- Server-side p95 (inference only): target < 250ms.
- End-to-end client-observed p95 (including network): target < 350ms.
We’ll document how we measure both and share our measurement script.

Below is a high-level integration plan and implementation notes for your engineering team. Dev / Dylan — please chime in if anything here is off.

Integration summary (developer-facing)- SDKs: Redwood provides an official JavaScript SDK and a lightweight REST API. For the webchat use case we recommend the SDK with streaming enabled (server-to-client chunked streaming to reduce perceived latency).

- API routes of interest:
  - POST /v1/generate — synchronous generation (good for short completions)
  - POST /v1/stream — server-side streaming endpoint (chunked responses for low-latency UX)
  - POST /v1/function_call — structured tool-calling path if Acme wants to call internal tools (e.g., search, ticket lookup) as part of generation

- Auth: API keys for the trial; for private deployments we can swap to mTLS or customer KMS-backed keys.

- SDK integration steps (suggested):
  1) Install redwood-js SDK (npm i @redwood/inference).
  2) Create a server-side proxy route to hold API keys; do not expose keys to browser.
  3) Use /v1/stream with SSE or WebSocket transport to send tokens to client quickly.
  4) Implement prefix caching on repeated prompts to reduce tokens.
  5) If you need external tool calls, implement a function registry and use /v1/function_call with agreed JSON schema.

- Observability: enable per-request tracing headers (x-redwood-trace) and send sample logs to our console so we can correlate latency spikes.

- Typical blockers we’ve seen: CORS/socket proxy, client reconnection handling, and oversized prompt serialization. Dylan/Dev — we can draft a short checklist for each.

Attachments included: updated integration checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx). Also linking the MOU template here: https://redwood.app/hubspot/engagements/12345

Next steps
1) Jordan/Priya — confirm kickoff for Tue 2026-03-10 10am PT and internal owner for signing the MOU.
2) Dev/Dylan — please confirm SDK compatibility and list any required infra we should plan for (proxy, SSE relay, auth).
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min dev-focused sync right after kickoff to walk the SDK sample and streaming flow.

Marissa
